title: Prambanan (Candi Siwa and the Loro Jonggrang temples)
summary: Prambanan, on the plain east of Yogyakarta in Java, is the largest Hindu temple compound in Indonesia. Three main temples to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma rise at its centre, with relief carvings of the Ramayana. The Shiva temple, about 47 m tall, was built in the 9th to 10th century CE.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO's list page says the compound was built in the 10th century, while its description dates Loro Jonggrang to the 9th century; the start 850 sits in the stated 9th-10th century span (801 to 1000). End is the present: the temples stand.

when.display: Built in the 9th–10th century CE; standing today

phases.description: UNESCO dates the compound to the 10th century (list page) and Loro Jonggrang to the 9th century (description); exact years are not in the sources opened.
The temples remain standing and are a World Heritage property; the sources opened give no dated collapse or restoration, so this phase is bridged.

reviewer_note: Shape tower (a tall pointed temple on a stepped square base; stepped_pyramid was the alternative). Height 47 m is from a tourism ministry page and is widely quoted; the 27.5 m base is from one reference site's survey summary, not a heritage body, so it is the least certain. The 'intact' phase is bridged; earthquake damage is not recorded here.
